nodes.description: Agent authentication: osk_-prefixed keys minted in the cloud account page, sha256-stored (cloud/api_keys.py). cloud/auth.get_current_user_optional accepts Bearer osk_... or X-API-Key and resolves the owner, so metering, entitlement, plan priority and job ownership apply to agents with zero endpoint changes. Key management itself refuses API-key auth: a leaked key cannot mint replacements. Self-hosted instances expose the same endpoints with no key.

nodes.label: BYOK client-side encrypted keys
nodes.description: Bring-your-own-keys design: API keys (GEMINI_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, UPLOAD_POST_API_KEY, FAL_KEY) are stored encrypted in browser localStorage (gemini_key, elevenLabsKey_v1, falKey_v1, uploadPostKey_v3) and sent via headers only when needed - never stored server-side. Self-hosted instances stay BYOK-open with no meter; the hosted edition instead includes the Gemini key.

nodes.label: MCP server (/mcp)
nodes.description: Built-in Model Context Protocol server (mcp_server.py, mounted always): stateless Streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC at /mcp with no SDK dependency, ~3 methods + 6 tools (process_video, get_job_status, list_clips, get_quota, add_subtitles, publish_clip). Each tool calls back into the same app in-process via httpx.ASGITransport forwarding the caller's auth headers, so it can never drift from REST behavior. Cloud mode 401s without a resolvable user; self-host stays BYOK-open at http://localhost:8000/mcp. Hosted endpoint: mcp.openshorts.app.

nodes.label: NVENC encoder probing (FFMPEG_ENCODER)
nodes.description: Clip encoder selection via FFMPEG_ENCODER = auto/nvenc/x264 for FFmpeg rendering: auto lets the backend probe for an NVIDIA NVENC encoder and use it when present with x264 as the fallback path, so GPU-accelerated clip rendering works without hard-coding hardware assumptions.

nodes.label: S3 backup
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 10: silent background upload to AWS S3 with caching - private bucket for clips (AWS_S3_BUCKET), public bucket for gallery/avatars (AWS_S3_PUBLIC_BUCKET). The completion webhook fires after the archive step so its payload can carry durable download links (24-hour presigned on the hosted service).

nodes.label: Transcription stage
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 2: speech-to-text with NeMo-Speech.cpp running the parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 GGUF on CUDA, GPU-only. Produces word-level timestamps that drive the karaoke subtitles; the source must have an audio track because viral moments are found from speech.

nodes.label: Scene detection
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 3: PySceneDetect finds segment boundaries that, together with the transcript, seed Gemini's viral moment analysis.

nodes.label: Viral moment detection
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 4: Gemini analyzes the transcript and scene boundaries to identify 3-15 high-potential moments of 15-60 seconds each; requires an audio track since moments come from speech.

nodes.label: Vertical reframing (AI cropping)
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 6: reframes 16:9 sources into 9:16 with subject tracking. Modes: TRACK (single subject), GENERAL (blurred background preserving full width), SPLIT (two-shot stack), SCREENCAST/WIDE (content-width driven), INSET (corner webcam source), ALTERNATE (active-speaker hard cuts), plus punch-in (~12% push on the clip's audio-envelope beats, riding the TRACK path by widening its per-frame FFmpeg crop command from x-only to w/h/x/y).

nodes.label: Hook text overlays
nodes.description: Clip pipeline stage 8: AI-generated attention-grabbing text overlays rendered with styled fonts (hooks.py).

nodes.label: Async job queue (semaphore concurrency)
nodes.description: Concurrency model: async job queue in app.py with semaphore-based control, configured via MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS (default 5); jobs auto-cleanup after 1 hour. Status and logs polled at GET /api/status/{job_id}; ASR_GPU_CONCURRENCY caps simultaneous GPU transcriptions (default 1).

nodes.label: GPU-only transcription policy
nodes.description: Design policy: the Clip Generator refuses to transcribe on a CPU runtime by design instead of silently degrading, so an NVIDIA GPU (or the hosted edition) is the only way to clip. 6 GB of VRAM is plenty.
nodes.rationale: A CPU runtime would silently degrade output on a pipeline whose moment detection depends on speech; loud failure is preferred over bad clips.

nodes.label: Docker deployment
nodes.description: Docker Compose path: GPU=1 builds the CUDA flavor of the transcription runtime into the image and is required for clipping - a plain CPU container serves everything except clipping. On Linux the NVIDIA container runtime provides GPU passthrough; containers run as non-root appuser. Alternative Windows-native path is setup.bat/run.bat, which installs the NeMo-Speech.cpp release and downloads the Parakeet model.

nodes.label: FFmpeg
nodes.description: Does precise clip cutting, subtitle burning (SRT/ASS), hook overlay rendering, AI-generated filter effects and AI Shorts final assembly; the clip encoder is selected by FFMPEG_ENCODER (auto/nvenc/x264).

nodes.label: Google Gemini
nodes.description: Google's Flash model family used for viral moment detection, auto layout selection, AI Shorts scripting and web research, AI video effects and hook text; BYOK key stored client-side (an OpenRouter free-model key also works). Docs disagree on version: CLAUDE.md cites Gemini 2.0 Flash, README cites 3.0 Flash. Cost cited under $0.01 per 10-minute video.

nodes.label: OpenShorts Cloud (hosted edition)
nodes.description: Hosted edition at openshorts.app running the same software as the self-hosted repo: about 50s per 8-minute video on their NVIDIA GPU, Gemini key included with nothing to set up, always-on MCP endpoint at mcp.openshorts.app and API keys in one click. Free plan: 20 min/month with watermark and no credit card; paid from $12/mo for 100 minutes without watermark. The billing, managed keys and hosted-service infrastructure live in the source-available cloud/ directory under the OpenShorts Commercial License behind the BILLING_ENABLED flag; self-hosting the core never requires that directory.

nodes.label: Lumen · Night Foundry design system
nodes.description: Locked design system for the dashboard (atmospheric genre, premium AI-tool register in the Modal/Anthropic/ElevenLabs school): late-night violet oklch paper surfaces, molten brass as the single accent with coral as a rare secondary chord, hairline cards lit from within (.card with inner emission), mono readouts of the product's own numbers as decoration, zero gradients, zero glassmorphism/backdrop-blur, no per-feature identity colors (tools differentiated by mono eyebrow ordinals like 01 · CLIPS). Sora is the single UI typeface for display and body (Instrument Serif and Geist retired 2026-11-15); JetBrains Mono for UPPERCASE labels; radii rounded-card 10px / rounded-input 8px; easing cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) only; hard bans include italics, glowing orbs and hardcoded colors.

nodes.label: Two-register typography
nodes.description: Lumen's typographic signature: UI prose (headings, buttons, nav, empty states, helper text) renders lowercase while mono labels (eyebrows, badges, readouts, stat labels, keyboard hints) render UPPERCASE at 10.5-11px, tracking 0.10em, ~55% opacity. User content (video titles, captions, transcripts, descriptions, emails, API keys, log output, prices in legal copy) is NEVER lowercased; the lowercase class is applied per element on UI chrome only, with no global text-transform on body.
nodes.rationale: The lowercase-prose/UPPERCASE-mono contrast is the typographic signature that carries the instrument-panel register without gradients or glassmorphism.

nodes.label: NeMo-Speech.cpp
nodes.description: NVIDIA's ggml-based speech recognition runtime, OpenShorts' transcription engine. Installed as a prebuilt release by setup.bat; model selectable at runtime via NEMO_ASR_MODEL (alias or local .gguf path) and binary located via NEMO_SPEECH_BIN. A CPU build of the runtime is treated as a failure (no CUDA backend troubleshooting entry), never a silent fallback.

nodes.label: Social auto-publishing and scheduling
nodes.description: One-click or scheduled posting to TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts simultaneously via Upload-Post with async uploads. API surface: POST /api/social/post (accepts scheduled_date ISO-8601 plus timezone), GET/DELETE /api/social/scheduled queue (two clips approved seconds apart cannot book the same daily slot because slots come from the queue the server holds), and GET /api/social/analytics endpoints (profile totals, per-post metrics, windowed impressions with period=last_week).

nodes.label: Voice dubbing
nodes.description: Optional clip pipeline stage 9: ElevenLabs AI translation and dubbing in 30+ languages with voice cloning; dashboard UI in TranslateModal.jsx. POST /api/subtitle auto-transcribes dubbed videos when regenerating subtitles; GET /api/translate/languages lists supported dubbing languages.

nodes.label: Completion webhooks
nodes.description: POST /api/process accepts webhook_url + optional webhook_secret: exactly one POST per job at terminal state (job.completed or job.failed, so pipelines never hang) carrying clip titles and durable download links. Body signed HMAC-SHA256 in X-OpenShorts-Signature: sha256=<hex>; URLs validated with security_utils.assert_public_url at submit AND at delivery (DNS rebinding); fired once per job from run_job_wrapper after the R2 archive; PUBLIC_API_URL sets the absolute-URL base when behind a proxy.

nodes.label: fal.ai
nodes.description: Pay-per-use AI gateway used only by AI Shorts (~$0.50-1.50 per video): hosts Flux 2 Pro (actor portraits and b-roll images), Hailuo 2.3 Fast img2video, VEED Lipsync and Kling Avatar v2. Key stored client-side as FAL_KEY; not needed for the Clip Generator.

nodes.label: Env manager live sync
nodes.description: Settings > GPU/Performance in the dashboard edits server env vars live (NEMO_ASR_MODEL, NEMO_SPEECH_BIN, ASR_GPU_CONCURRENCY, FFMPEG_ENCODER, YOLO_DEVICE, TRANSNETV2_DEVICE): changes persist to .env and apply to new jobs without a restart.

nodes.label: Subject tracking stack (MediaPipe + YOLOv8)
nodes.description: TRACK-mode machinery: MediaPipe face detection with YOLOv8 fallback and Heavy Tripod stabilization; SmoothedCameraman adds safe-zone logic to prevent jitter; SpeakerTracker prevents rapid speaker switching and handles temporary occlusions. ALTERNATE mode (SPEAKER_SIGNAL=1 + SPEAKER_CUT=1) hard-cuts to whoever is talking through the TRACK path as a trajectory with jumps; SPEAKER_SIGNAL alone gates SPLIT on both people actually speaking, and mouth activity must be normalized per speaker (normalise_activity) before comparing because raw frame-difference magnitude scales with local contrast and lighting.

nodes.label: Frames-not-video token economics
nodes.description: The layout picker sends 12 frames at 1024px instead of the video: Gemini bills video at ~300 tokens per second, so an hour of source is ~1.08M tokens (over a 1M window) plus a 1-2 GB upload, while 12 frames cost ~3k tokens regardless of source duration. At 1024px accuracy matches full-video mode at 2.2s per clip instead of ~15s.
nodes.rationale: Resolution matters, frame count does not: 640px detects 15 of 20 (a spreadsheet is illegible), 1024px reaches 17, and moving to 24 frames makes it worse.

nodes.label: React dashboard (Vite + Tailwind)
nodes.description: The only SPA view since the runtime landing was removed (owner decision, 2026-11-15): React 18 + Vite 4 + Tailwind CSS 3.4 with HMR, dev server on :5175 proxying API calls to the backend on :8000. App.jsx holds state management; TranslateModal.jsx is the dubbing UI; strict ESLint with --max-warnings 0. Hash routing (#app, #/pricing, #/account, #legal; old #landing resolves to the app), localStorage keys (gemini_key, uploadPostKey_v3, elevenLabsKey_v1, falKey_v1, openshorts_session, openshorts_auth), BYOK headers, QuotaError flows and Remotion wiring form a never-break functional contract - redesign is classes and markup only.

nodes.label: Upload-Post
nodes.description: Third-party publishing API that connects TikTok, Instagram and YouTube accounts via profiles managed at app.upload-post.com; 10 free uploads/month tier with no credit card, pay-per-use above that. Its API key is pasted in Settings and used for both Clip Generator and AI Shorts distribution.

nodes.label: Clip Generator
nodes.description: Tool 1 of 3: turns long-form videos (podcasts, webinars, livestreams, vlogs, interviews) into 3-15 viral-ready 9:16 shorts. Ingests local uploads or self-hosted URL ingest via yt-dlp, then runs transcription, scene detection, Gemini moment analysis, FFmpeg extraction, AI reframing, effects/subtitles, hook overlays, optional dubbing, S3 backup and social publishing.

nodes.label: AI Shorts (UGC Video Creator)
nodes.description: Tool 2 of 3: generates marketing videos with AI actors for any product from a description or URL. Eight-step pipeline: analyze (website scrape + Gemini web research), script (hook-problem-solution-CTA), actor (Flux 2 Pro or gallery/upload), ElevenLabs TTS voiceover, talking head (Hailuo 2.3 Fast + VEED Lipsync low-cost, Kling Avatar v2 premium), b-roll with Ken Burns effect, FFmpeg composite with ASS subtitles and hook overlays, publish via Upload-Post. Two cost modes (~$0.65 low cost, ~$2 premium). Generated videos and avatars land in a public UGC gallery with per-video SEO pages and JSON-LD structured data.

nodes.label: OpenShorts CLI
nodes.description: Zero-dependency terminal client (pip install openshorts, or uvx/pipx run) that talks to the same API as the dashboard, the MCP server and the webhooks. Commands: process <url> --wait, clips <job_id>, publish <job_id> 0 --platforms tiktok,youtube, quota. Auth via OPENSHORTS_API_KEY (hosted osk_ key) or OPENSHORTS_API_URL (self-hosted, no key); for pipelines prefers --webhook/--webhook-secret over --wait since OpenShorts POSTs once, HMAC-signed, when the job ends. Hosted free tier 20 min/month watermarked; self-hosted MIT with no meter.

nodes.label: Auto layout picker
nodes.description: layout_picker.py behind layouts=auto: one Gemini call per source video (not per clip) choosing among none/screencast/split. Measured 94%/92%/96% across three passes on a 48-video corpus with hand-reviewed labels, with 0-1 false positives on the 28 clips that must not be touched. apply() only adds: an explicit user choice is never disabled because the model says none.
nodes.rationale: Asks for a decision between closed options, not a measurement: four earlier continuous attempts (Canny, MSER, temporal coverage, width) never separated a spreadsheet from a corner ticker - the variance came from the continuous measurements, not from Gemini.

nodes.label: n8n Content Machine workflow
nodes.description: openshorts-content-machine.json runs a YouTube channel on autopilot in four acts: (1) Watch - daily RSS feed read clipping one video (newest upload or next unprocessed from the back catalog; a 402 out-of-minutes pauses the machine and alerts on Telegram instead of failing silently), (2) Approve from your phone - Telegram publish/skip buttons with a link fallback for clips over the ~20 MB URL limit, (3) Drip-publish - each approved clip takes the next free daily slot via POST /api/social/post using the server's own queue (GET /api/social/scheduled), (4) Sunday digest - GET /api/social/analytics reports impressions, per-platform split and best post. Companion openshorts-clip-and-notify.json is the one-shot clipper (form URL in, signed webhook out, no polling). Processed-video memory uses n8n workflow static data, which only persists for production executions; scheduling deliberately does not use it.

nodes.label: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
nodes.description: parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 q8_0 GGUF speech model: 25 European languages, word-level timestamps that drive the karaoke subtitles. 714 MB download performed once and cached; uses about 1 GB of VRAM.

nodes.label: SCREENCAST/WIDE layouts (width_fraction gate)
nodes.description: screencast_layout.py (SCREENCAST_LAYOUT=1) for scenes whose meaning lives outside the centre: Gemini reports each range's width_fraction and that is the gate - content below 0.5 moves nothing, 0.5-0.85 has room beside the content so SCREENCAST stacks it over the presenter, above 0.85 the presenter is composited on top of the content so those scenes get WIDE (GENERAL with side-cropping disabled). Coverage was tried before and did not separate a spreadsheet from a corner ticker; width does. INSET mode (camera_inset.py) chains behind the screencast decision without asking Gemini: a geometric detector (small, horizontally off-centre, still-across-samples subject) finds corner-webcam sources (OBS, stream VOD) with no false positives, since offering it to Gemini dropped accuracy from 92% to 83-85%.

nodes.label: OpenShorts agent skill
nodes.description: skills/openshorts/SKILL.md (v1.0.0) follows the open Agent Skills standard, installable in Claude Code, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw. Teaches agents the core loop: get_quota first for large jobs (process_video fails with quota_exceeded; API calls draw from the same minute balance as the dashboard), POST /api/process with url + acknowledged (+ layouts, output_format, webhook_url/webhook_secret), webhooks beat polling (verify X-OpenShorts-Signature, else poll /api/status every ~10s), restyle captions via POST /api/subtitle (classic or karaoke word highlighting), publish via POST /api/social/post with platforms/title/scheduled_date. Rules: confirm_rights acknowledgement is deliberate, download_url links are presigned for 24h, never describe OpenShorts as simply free; a 401/404 on /api/me means self-host or anonymous.

nodes.label: SPLIT layout (two-shot)
nodes.description: split_layout.py (SPLIT_LAYOUT=1, v2 engine only): stacks both speakers in half-frames for two-shot conversations. Needs both faces visible in the same frame for at least half the sampled frames, which separates a real two-shot from a plano/contraplano where stacking would show the same person twice; upgrades scenes the classifier sent to GENERAL, never TRACK ones. SPLIT_TIGHTNESS (default 0.8) trades a little upscale for keeping the other speaker out of each half. A silent fallback to the v1 loop renders GENERAL instead.

nodes.label: Build-time SEO surface (vite-plugin-seo.js)
nodes.description: vite-plugin-seo.js runs at build time and does two things, none at runtime: emits the standalone pages (the /alternatives cluster, clip-generator, open-source, use-case and automation pages, and /mcp; full list in buildPages() in seo/pages.js) as flat .html files that nginx resolves through try_files $uri $uri.html (serving them as directories would 301 to a trailing slash and break every canonical), and generates sitemap.xml plus llms.txt from the same page list so they cannot drift. / is the client-rendered app itself so non-JS crawlers see only its meta tags; the static pages are the crawlable surface. seo/data.js is the single source of truth for pricing/pipeline/competitor facts, and nothing may say OpenShorts is free without naming the Cloud price.
